note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor (authored none of the userns spec commits d8427e4380, b00e3c6710, 68b723ec4f, 7d11a51269). userns.Enter (internal/test/userns/userns_linux.go) re-executes the one test in a new user+net+mount namespace and returns false in the parent only after the child's own PASS line; a child failure, a zero-exit failure or a child that selected nothing fails the parent, and a child skip skips it, so the guard cannot turn a red into a green. Section 7.2: "A traffic-rate-packets of 0 should result in all traffic for the particular flow to be discarded." TestSelectedFlowSpecZeroPacketRateKernel changed by the guard and by namespace get/create failing instead of skipping (stronger); its RFC-approved judge line is in b00e3c6710. Assertions unchanged: literal 0x800c rate zero through the selected callback into real nft discards four target packets with exact 4-packet/116-byte counters, another destination is delivered, positive-rate replacement and withdrawal restore target delivery, and the reinstall/token sequence distinguishes stale zero-rate enforcement from removal. Zero-rate needs no nft payload write, so it runs in the user namespace (the DSCP test that needs one stays privileged). Mutant records (rate==0 condition both ways) re-taken in b00e3c6710 and current. Local IPv4 input only, not VPN or transit dataplane.
